incentives.name: Data Center Enterprise tax exemptions (standard statewide program)
incentives.law: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 57-113-21 et seq. (thresholds lowered in 2019)
incentives.what: MDA-certified data centers get a 10-year sales and use tax exemption on initial construction materials and equipment, plus state income and franchise tax exemptions. To qualify: MDA approval, at least $20 million investment, at least 20 full-time jobs paying 125% of the state average wage. Contract has recapture (clawback) clauses and annual review. In 2019 the Legislature cut the thresholds from $50M / 50 jobs / 150% of average wage. Used by xAI, Compass and AVAIO per Mississippi Today.

incentives.name: Project Atlas incentive package for Amazon Web Services (Mississippi Major Economic Impact Act)
incentives.law: Senate Bill 2001, 2024 Second Extraordinary Session (amends Sec. 57-75-5 and related sections; approved by Governor 2024-01-30)
incentives.what: Special-session package written for a data center project of at least $10 billion and 1,000 jobs paying at least 125% of state average wage (only AWS qualifies so far). Includes sales tax exemption on equipment purchases (described by Mississippi Today as permanent), sales tax exemption on electricity and fuel bought by the project, income tax exemption for income from the data center project, fee-in-lieu of franchise tax and fee-in-lieu of ad valorem (property) tax authority for Madison County, state general obligation bonds, and clawback provisions.
incentives.value_known: $44 million in state appropriations (mostly workforce training) plus a $215 million state loan to Madison County for roads, water and sewer, repaid from AWS fee-in-lieu payments (Mississippi Today). State economist estimated $41.3M state revenue during construction and $153.7M over first 15 years of operation.

incentives.name: Fee-in-lieu of ad valorem (property) tax agreements
incentives.law: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 27-31-104 (and SB 2001 2024 2nd Ex. Sess. for AWS)
incentives.what: Counties and cities can let a data center pay as little as one-third of the property taxes otherwise owed. Agreements start once at least $60 million is invested and the center is running; up to 30 years overall, each piece of property up to 10 years. Madison County ties the AWS fee to benchmarks (700 jobs by 2036, $10B invested by 2030) and is the only county that publishes estimated payments.
incentives.value_known: AWS to pay an estimated $28 million to Madison County in 2027; over $1 billion estimated to local bodies in first 10 years (Mississippi Today).

incentives.name: Compass Datacenters Meridian (Lauderdale County) - standard data center program plus state site grant
incentives.law: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 57-113-21 et seq. (standard program); no special session or project-specific law found
incentives.what: MDA certification as a data center enterprise: 10-year state corporate income and franchise tax exemptions and sales and use tax exemption on construction materials, equipment and hardware/software replacements. State also gave site-prep help including a $4 million site grant. Mississippi Power serves the site under a PSC-approved special contract (docket 2025-UN-3). Mississippi Today (2026-07-29) reports the Center for Economic Accountability named it the 'Worst Economic Development Deal of the Year'.
incentives.value_known: $4 million state site grant; value of tax exemptions not disclosed

incentives.name: AVAIO Digital Taurus campus (Brandon, Rankin County) - standard data center program
incentives.law: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 57-113-21 et seq.; no special session or project-specific law found (separate 2026 SB 3410 covers Brandon/West Rankin water deals)
incentives.what: MDA approved the Data Center Enterprises sales and use tax exemption; MDA Site Development Grant to the industrial park and MDA help to Brandon and Rankin County. Company sought a fee-in-lieu of property tax from county supervisors.

incentives.name: xAI Southaven (DeSoto County) - data center incentive plus local fee-in-lieu
incentives.law: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 57-113-21 et seq.; fee-in-lieu under Sec. 27-31-104
incentives.what: MDA data center incentive (sales and use tax exemption on computing equipment and software) plus fee-in-lieu of property tax agreements with the City of Southaven and DeSoto County.

incentives.name: AWS Vicksburg (Warren County) - uses 2024 SB 2001 framework
incentives.law: SB 2001 (2024 2nd Ex. Sess.), Mississippi Major Economic Impact Act
incentives.what: State says the Warren County AWS campus falls under the 2024 Project Atlas legislation; Warren County contributes; MDA said no additional state funds were needed.

incentives.name: AWS Clinton (Hinds County) - local fee-in-lieu agreement
incentives.law: Fee-in-lieu of ad valorem taxes (Sec. 27-31-104); MMEIA funds
incentives.what: Fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement approved by the Clinton Board of Aldermen and Hinds County Board of Supervisors (Jan. 15, 2026), plus Major Economic Impact Authority funds. Amounts not published.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 2001 (2024 Second Extraordinary Session) - AWS Project Atlas package and Section 22 large customer supply and service agreements
laws_and_bills.what: Major Economic Impact Act package for AWS data centers (see incentives). Section 22, codified at Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 77-3-271, lets Entergy Mississippi sign a 'large customer supply and service agreement' with such a project and grants the utility a certificate of public convenience and necessity for power plants, lines and substations needed to serve it; the utility only files informational notices at the PSC. (Entergy's PSC filings, e.g. docket 2024-UA-144, call the agreements trade secrets exempt from the Public Records Act; see dockets.) Passed Senate and House 2024-01-25; approved by Governor 2024-01-30.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 3106 (2024) - revise data center enterprise tax exemption definitions
laws_and_bills.what: Would have revised definitions of 'business enterprise' and 'data center' for the Sec. 57-113 exemptions and given 60 days to cure noncompliance before losing exemption. Passed Senate 2024-03-27; died in House Ways and Means 2024-04-16.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 1641 (2024) - exempt economic development project records from Public Records Act
laws_and_bills.what: Would have exempted public-body records with client information about economic development projects from the Public Records Act. Passed House; died on Senate calendar 2024-04-10.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 2811 (2024) - exempt economic development project records from Public Records Act
laws_and_bills.what: Would have kept economic development project records secret during review and negotiation. Died in Senate committee 2024-03-05.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 1184 (2025) - expand large customer supply and service agreements
laws_and_bills.what: Would have created Sec. 77-3-273 letting certain utilities sign large customer supply and service agreements with any customer whose project MDA approves as meeting capital investment and job minimums (extending the AWS-style setup beyond SB 2001). Passed House Public Utilities committee as amended; died on House calendar 2025-02-13.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 2488 (2025) - exempt economic development project records from Public Records Act
laws_and_bills.what: Same idea as 2024 SB 2811. Died in Senate committee 2025-02-04.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 1239 (2025) - data center enterprise tax exemption changes
laws_and_bills.what: Would have revised definitions and application contents for the Sec. 57-113 data center exemptions and added a 60-day cure period. Died in conference 2025-03-29.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 3168 (2025) - data center enterprise tax exemption extensions
laws_and_bills.what: Would have made data centers automatically eligible for up to two more 10-year exemption extensions for expansions, including hardware replacement, applied for directly at the Department of Revenue. Passed Senate 2025-02-26; died in House committee 2025-03-18.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 1635 (2026) - share of big-project fee-in-lieu to a state fund
laws_and_bills.what: For projects over $1 billion with fee-in-lieu deals signed after 2026-07-01, part of the fee on the amount above $1 billion would go to a new Mississippi Strategic Development Fund run by MDA. Sponsor Rep. Trey Lamar. Died in House Ways and Means 2026-02-03.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 4045 (2026) - end data center project income tax exemption after 2026
laws_and_bills.what: Would have ended the income tax exemption for certain data center projects after calendar year 2026, revised the Major Economic Impact Act project definition, and sent part of fee-in-lieu on projects over $2 billion to a Mississippi Strategic Development Fund. Passed Ways and Means 2026-02-24; died on House calendar 2026-02-25.

laws_and_bills.name: HB 1534 (2026) - Mississippi Energy Security and Agricultural Growth Act
laws_and_bills.what: Not data-center specific. Would have defined clean energy to include advanced and renewable natural gas and provided for 'protection of ratepayer affordability'. Died on House calendar 2026-02-12. Companion SB 2922 died in committee.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 3410 (2026) - Brandon and West Rankin Utility Authority water deals with data centers
laws_and_bills.what: Lets the City of Brandon and West Rankin Utility Authority contract with a data center developer for water and wastewater infrastructure that the developer pays for on a progress-payment basis, and allows delivery of reclaimed water for cooling. Tied to Rankin County data center (AVAIO area). Approved by Governor 2026-04-08.

regulators.name: Mississippi Public Service Commission (PSC)
regulators.role: Regulates investor-owned electric utilities (Entergy Mississippi, Mississippi Power) and electric power associations' service areas and certificates; reviews special contracts and data center power agreements; receives Section 22 informational filings. Docket search at ctsportal.psc.ms.gov.

regulators.name: Mississippi Public Utilities Staff
regulators.role: Separate state agency that represents the public interest in PSC cases and makes recommendations on utility filings.

regulators.name: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) / Environmental Quality Permit Board
regulators.role: Air permits for on-site gas turbines and generators (e.g. xAI Southaven), water withdrawal (surface and groundwater) permits through Office of Land and Water Resources, wastewater (NPDES) and stormwater permits.

regulators.name: Mississippi Development Authority (MDA)
regulators.role: State economic development agency. Certifies data center enterprises for tax exemptions, negotiates incentive contracts, administers Major Economic Impact Act funds and site grants.

regulators.name: Mississippi Major Economic Impact Authority (MMEIA)
regulators.role: Unit inside MDA that carries out special-session projects such as AWS Project Atlas (SB 2001, 2024).

regulators.name: Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)
regulators.role: Federal power agency. Sets wholesale and retail rates for its local power companies in north and east Mississippi (not regulated by the PSC) and its local power companies' service to large loads (e.g. TVA reviewed the proposed Starkville crypto mine's grid impact).

regulators.name: Mississippi Department of Revenue
regulators.role: Administers sales, use, income and franchise tax exemptions for certified data centers.

rate_cases.what: Delta Blues Advanced Power Station: new combined cycle gas plant in Washington County, built under Sec. 77-3-271 (no PSC certificate case) to serve AWS (docket 2024-UA-144).
Vicksburg Advanced Power Station: new combined cycle gas plant in Warren County tied to the AWS Warren County campus (docket 2025-AD-123).

Traceview Advanced Power Station: new combined cycle gas plant in Madison County tied to AWS agreements (docket 2026-UA-55); plus Penton Solar 190 MW (2026-UA-54) and Delta Solar 80 MW (2026-UA-56) filed the same day.

Synapse Energy report for Environmental Advocates Mississippi and Earthjustice ('In the Dark'): residential customers paid $38 million by March 2026 for grid upgrades that appear to serve data centers, with $80 million more expected by end of 2026; 'Superpower Mississippi' grid program expected to cost $300 million over five years. Entergy disputes the findings.
rate_cases.impact: Estimate: residential bills up to $10.60/month higher (Synapse estimate, kind=estimate)

rate_cases.what: 2026 formula rate plan (docket 2025-UN-112) approved by PSC; Entergy says new data center revenue prevented a July increase, and it filed for a further $0.41/month cut (ad valorem tax adjustment, partly due to data center revenue) to take effect in October if approved. Entergy cites more than $2 billion in projected customer savings over 20 years under its 'Fair Share Plus Pledge'.
Entergy testimony to the state AI regulation task force: residential bills projected to be $30/month lower by 2030 than without data center growth. PSC Commissioner De'Keither Stamps also testified.
rate_cases.impact: Projected -$30/month by 2030 vs. no-data-center case (Entergy projection, kind=estimate)

rate_cases.what: To power the Compass Datacenters Meridian campus, Mississippi Power told the PSC (2025-01-09) it must delay closing at least one Plant Daniel coal unit (Jackson County), and possibly other fossil steam units, until the mid-2030s; PSC unanimously approved the Compass special contract (docket 2025-UN-3). Plant had been slated to close its coal units by 2027-2028.

New transmission and 230 kV substation to serve Compass's ~500 MW Meridian load (docket 2025-UA-25), estimated $117 million over 2025-2032; Mississippi Power pays upfront with part offset by a Compass contribution-in-aid-of-construction, and says the contract is designed to recover the investment.

local_rules.what: City Council approved a 183-day citywide moratorium on data center zoning changes and permits, 5-2, the first in Mississippi. Took effect 30 days later because the vote was not unanimous. Council can extend or end it; during the pause it will pick suitable sites and study impacts. Triggered by a proposed data center on Forest Avenue in northwest Jackson. Sources differ on the second 'no' vote (Hartley vs. Parkinson); Ashby Foote voted no.
Vote on rezoning Forest Avenue property for a data center postponed while the city works to amend its zoning ordinance to cover data centers.

Board of Aldermen unanimously amended the zoning ordinance: adds a data center definition (incl. crypto mining, AI training and cloud storage), requires a conditional use permit, limits data centers to I-1 and I-2 industrial zones. More ordinances planned.

City approved rezoning of farmland for a proposed hyperscale data center; officials called it 'the beginning of the conversation'. Capital B News (https://capitalbnews.org/data-center-clarksdale-mississippi/) reports about 15 residents sued the city claiming improper public notice.

Planning and Zoning Commission denied a special use exemption for a bitcoin mining facility (Starkville Energy LLC; DatacenterDynamics reported up to 30 MW) at 407 Industrial Park Road; staff cited missing water, wastewater, jobs, flood and environmental information. The Unified Development Code does not list this use, so an exemption was needed even in an industrial zone. Company said it may try again.

Board of Aldermen approved the design plan for a 660,000 sq ft SpaceXAI/MZX Tech data center on the city's former 51-acre training site on Tulane Road (use allowed by right on industrial land). Ward 2 Alderman Charles Hoots voted no, citing turbine noise.

Federal class action (Haley v. X.AI Corp., N.D. Miss., filed 2026-06-08) by three Southaven residents alleges noise, vibration, nuisance and negligence from xAI's gas turbines; Memphis Flyer reports it claims violations of Southaven's noise ordinance (https://www.memphisflyer.com/lawsuit-targets-continuous-squealing-roaring-from-xais-southaven-center/).

Residents delivered a 950-signature petition to the Board of Supervisors asking for a temporary pause on data center construction (Big Woods Technology Park). County has no zoning; residents also asked for noise and air ordinances.

ballot_measures.what: None found: no state or county ballot measure on data centers found as of 2026-10-14. Ballotpedia's 2026 roundup of local data center ballot measures lists none in Mississippi.

polls.what: No Mississippi-specific public poll on data centers found as of 2026-10-14. National polls (e.g. Annenberg, Aug 2026: 61% oppose a data center nearby) are not state-specific.
